title: Stalks of the inverse image of a sheaf of sets along a continuous map, with germs
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of sets on $Y$. For a presheaf of sets $\mathcal P$ on a space $T$ and $t\in T$ let $\mathcal P_t=\varinjlim_{W\ni t}\mathcal P(W)$ be its stalk, the colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] over the open neighbourhoods $W$ of $t$ ordered by reverse inclusion, and $s\mapsto s_t$ the coprojection $\mathcal P(W)\to\mathcal P_t$ (the germ). Let $f_p\mathcal G(U)=\varinjlim_{V\supseteq f(U)}\mathcal G(V)$ ($V\subseteq Y$ open, colimit of sets) be the presheaf inverse image, with coprojections $\iota^U_V$, and $\theta:f_p\mathcal G\to f^{-1}\mathcal G$ its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets; for $V\subseteq Y$ open and $s\in\mathcal G(V)$ put $\eta_V(s)=\theta_{f^{-1}V}(\iota^{f^{-1}V}_V(s))\in(f^{-1}\mathcal G)(f^{-1}V)$. Then for every $x\in X$, with $y=f(x)$, there is exactly one map of sets $c:\mathcal G_y\to(f^{-1}\mathcal G)_x$ with $c(s_y)=(\eta_V(s))_x$ for every open $V\ni y$ and every $s\in\mathcal G(V)$, and $c$ is bijective.
